note:
ISO 2026-W08 runs from February 16 through February 22. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌑 New Moon — 12:01:09 UTC. The dark Moon favors faint targets and extended star fields. Use Adhara, Wezen as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: In solar glare; magnitude -5.8; direct motion; 2.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Feb 17 12:01 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Feb 18 23:08 UTC. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Feb 18 08:01 UTC. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Feb 16 18:09 UTC. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Feb 21 09:51 UTC. Conjunction with Saturn in ecliptic longitude Feb 19 20:48 UTC. Conjunction with Neptune in ecliptic longitude Feb 19 20:55 UTC. story_candidates.dek: Adhara is a stellar reference in CMa used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Adhara for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved CMa constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
